title: How to Migrate from Glide Classic to GlideOS: Why It's Really a Rebuild
summary: Can you migrate a Glide Classic app to GlideOS? Not directly. Check before you move.
body_markdown:
Your Glide app has run part of the business for years. Field crews log jobs in it, the office checks progress, and a few subcontractors open it to see their next site visit. Then Glide announces GlideOS, and someone asks the obvious question: how do we move our app over?


I've spoken with a lot of operations leads asking exactly that, and the honest answer surprises most of them. You can't move it. GlideOS is a separate product, so getting there means rebuilding your app from scratch. And if you're rebuilding anyway, it's worth asking whether GlideOS is the right place to rebuild, or whether your app has grown into something that needs a different home.


## TL;DR


- In June 2026, Glide launched GlideOS, an AI builder, and renamed its original visual builder Glide Classic.
- There's no migration path. Glide Classic and GlideOS have separate subscriptions, separate apps, and can't share app data. Moving means rebuilding.
- Your Glide Classic app keeps working, so you don't have to act today. But Glide now points new signups to GlideOS.
- If you rebuild, list who uses the app first. If clients, subcontractors, or partners log in, check which plan lets outside people in and how you control what each person sees.
- Noloco lets you keep your Google Sheet or Airtable base, describe the app to AI, and give every team member, client, and partner their own login with only their own records.


## What changed when Glide launched GlideOS?


On June 4, 2026, Glide[announced GlideOS in beta](https://community.glideapps.com/t/introducing-glideos/87253) as "our new AI builder for internal business apps." In the same post, Glide said: "The Glide you've known for 7+ years is now Glide Classic, our visual no-code builder."


The two products work in very different ways. In Glide Classic, you build screens by dragging and setting up components. In GlideOS, you describe the app or upload a spreadsheet, and Glide's AI agent builds it. Every change after that happens by asking the agent in a chat. GlideOS plans are priced by team members and AI credits, while Glide Classic plans are priced by users and data updates. You can compare plans on[Glide's pricing page](https://www.glideapps.com/pricing) .


One naming trap to avoid: Glide Classic is not the same as Glide's old mobile "Classic Apps." Those were[shut down on June 30, 2025](https://www.glideapps.com/docs/reference/account/classic-apps) . If your app still opens today, you're on Glide Classic, the builder this article is about.


## Can you migrate a Glide Classic app to GlideOS?


No. Glide describes the two as "separate, co-existing platforms with their own teams, subscriptions, and apps," and its pricing page says GlideOS is "completely separate from the original Glide platform (Glide Classic)." In practice, that means four things for your business:


- **Separate subscriptions.** Paying for Glide Classic doesn't give you GlideOS. You need a second plan, and you pay for both while you run them side by side.
- **No automatic migration.** Your Classic apps don't transfer. When users asked about it in Glide's community, a long-time Glide expert called a migration feature "prob unlikely due to the vastly different architectures of the systems."
- **No shared data.** A GlideOS app can't read the data inside your Classic app. If your data lives in Glide's own tables, you'll need to get it out and connect it again.
- **A different way of building.** Everything you learned about Classic's editor doesn't carry over. You're learning a new product, not upgrading an old one.


Your Classic app is safe for now: Glide says apps built in Glide Classic "are unaffected by GlideOS." But if you'll need to rebuild at some point, it pays to plan the rebuild on your own schedule, not when something breaks.

## Should you stay on Glide Classic, rebuild in GlideOS, or switch?


It depends on what your app does today and who uses it. Here's how I'd think about it:


- **Stay on Glide Classic** if the app is simple, it works, and nothing about your process is changing. There's no prize for rebuilding early.
- **Rebuild in GlideOS** if the app is internal, only your own team uses it, and you like the idea of building by chatting with AI.
- **Switch to another platform** if outside people use the app, if different people need to see different records, or if the app has grown into the place where real work gets approved, assigned, and billed.


That third group is bigger than most people expect. An app that started as a job list for your own crew often ends up being opened by subcontractors, clients, or suppliers. That's exactly the point where the rebuild decision matters most.


## What should you check before you rebuild a Glide app?


Before you pick a platform, write down how the app is really used. Every message you send asking "has this been done?" is a sign of work the app should be doing. Across six European markets, employees spend around 15 hours a week on five core admin tasks, according to[Ricoh Europe's 2025 research](https://www.ricoh.se/nyheter-event/nyheter/leaders-recognise-admin-overload-employees-europe-lose-15-hours-week/) . A rebuild is your chance to take some of those hours back, not just copy the old screens.


Answer these five questions first:


- **Who logs in?** List your own team, then everyone outside it: clients, subcontractors, partners, suppliers. On GlideOS, the Basic plan publishes apps for your team only, and public apps start on the Plus plan.
- **What should each person see?** "A subcontractor sees only their own jobs and compliance documents" is the level of detail you need. Then check the plan: on GlideOS, org-level roles come with Pro, and project-level roles with Enterprise.
- **Where does the data live?** If it's in a Google Sheet or an Airtable base, it's already outside Glide. If it's in Glide's own tables, plan how you'll export it.
- **What happens automatically?** Write down every notification, approval, and status change the app handles today, so nothing gets lost in the rebuild.
- **Who changes the app?** If one person built it and everyone else depends on them, choose a platform the next person can also understand.

**5. Invite people in stages.** Log in as a test client and a test subcontractor before inviting anyone. Then run both apps side by side for a few weeks, and switch off the Classic app once everyone is using the new one.

## When is GlideOS the better choice?


I'd be doing you a disservice if I said Noloco is right for every Glide user. GlideOS makes sense if your app is used only by your own team, if the process is simple and doesn't change much, and if you're already comfortable with how Glide works. Glide has years of experience building apps for internal teams, and building from a chat is a fast way to get a first version.


Noloco is the stronger fit when the app is shared with people outside your business, when each person needs to see different records, or when the app holds work that gets approved, assigned, and billed. If you want a wider view of the options, read our guide to[Glide alternatives](https://noloco.io/blog/glide-alternatives) .


## Final thoughts


GlideOS isn't an upgrade to the app you already have. It's a new product, with its own subscription and no way to bring your Classic app with you. Your current app will keep working for now, so there's no need to panic, but there's also no shortcut.


Use the time to plan. List who logs in, what each person should see, where the data lives, and what happens automatically. If that list includes clients, or partners, rebuild somewhere designed for them from day one.

## Frequently asked questions


**Is Glide Classic being shut down?**
Glide hasn't announced an end date for Glide Classic. When it launched GlideOS in June 2026, Glide said apps built in Glide Classic are unaffected and that users can keep building as usual. Glide now points new signups to GlideOS, so it's worth planning ahead.


**Can I use my Glide Classic subscription for GlideOS?**
No. Glide Classic and GlideOS have separate subscriptions. If you want to try GlideOS while keeping your Classic app running, you'll pay for both plans.


**How do I move or convert my Glide Classic app to GlideOS? ‍** You can't move, convert, or copy a Glide Classic app into GlideOS, and its data doesn't transfer either. You rebuild the app in GlideOS by describing it or uploading a spreadsheet. If your data is in a Google Sheet or another outside source, connect that source again. If it's in Glide's own tables, export it first.


**What's the difference between Glide Classic and Glide's old Classic Apps?**
Classic Apps were Glide's original mobile apps, renamed in 2023 and shut down on June 30, 2025. Glide Classic is the name Glide gave its visual no-code builder in June 2026, when GlideOS launched. Glide Classic apps still work.


**How long does it take to rebuild a Glide app on another platform?**
It depends on how many user types, screens, and automatic steps your app has. Because GlideOS can't import your Classic app, you start from scratch wherever you rebuild, so it's worth comparing other platforms before you commit. On[Noloco](https://noloco.io/) , for example, you connect the Google Sheet or Airtable base your Glide app already uses (or more than one) and describe the app to Nola, its AI builder, which creates the pages, roles, and links between tables for you. Start with one group of users, test it, then add the next. You can even[do it from the AI subscription you're already paying for,](https://noloco.io/product/mcp?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=alternatives&utm_content=glide) that being Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or any other, so you save time and money.


**Can clients and contractors use an app built with an AI app builder?**
Yes, if the platform supports outside users and lets you control what each person sees. Check which plan allows public or external logins, and test as a client or contractor before inviting anyone.
